topic: A higher offer destroys your lower choices
text:
Ten ranked choices sounds generous, and the ranking behaves more sharply than in most systems. When offers are made, an offer on a higher choice causes every lower choice to fall away, and there is no wait-list for one that has gone.

So the order is not a preference, it is a decision made in advance. Putting a programme above another means accepting it if both would have taken you, with no opportunity to reconsider once the offer arrives. The last chance to get that order right is 1 July.
attribution: Samordna opptak’s own explanation of re-prioritisation
